Knit connects directly to nearby phones over Wi-Fi Aware to relay encrypted messages — no internet, no servers. It needs the nearby-devices permission to find peers, and works best when allowed to run in the background.

GitHub issues are public — anyone can read what you post. Knit removed ids, names and message text from this report before showing it to you, but read it over first. Your browser will open a bug form with the details filled in, and the full report will be on your clipboard to paste in.

Keep conversations flowing when nobody is in radio range, by storing sealed copies on relay servers. Relays cannot read your messages, but they do see that a conversation is active and the IP addresses connecting to it.
Turning this off stops new uploads. Sealed copies already on a relay are unreadable to it and expire within 48 hours.
No relays added. The Internet plane stays off until you add one — your messages still travel by Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
That relay is already in your list
Extend the reach of the Nearby room and your private messages over long-range LoRa by pairing a Meshtastic board over Bluetooth. Groups, typing and photos stay on the phone-to-phone radios.
Turning this off closes the board connection. Groups and attachments never travel over LoRa.

Direct messages stay end-to-end encrypted, but who is messaging whom, and when, is visible to any LoRa radio in range — kilometres, not metres. Turn this off to keep private messages on the phone-to-phone radios.

Adds the Knit channel, renames the board so you can spot it on the mesh, marks it unmonitored so other Meshtastic users aren\'t left messaging it, stops it broadcasting its position and node info, and stops it relaying other radios\' traffic. It stays on the public Meshtastic frequency, so other radios can still pass Knit messages along.

This board\'s main channel has been renamed, which puts its radio on a different frequency. Other Knit boards won\'t hear it. Set the main channel back to the default in the Meshtastic app.
This board is set to %1$s rather than this region\'s usual %2$s. Radios on different presets can\'t hear each other, so every other Knit board you want to reach has to be set to %1$s too.
Set this board up for Knit?

This adds the Knit channel to your board and changes a few of its settings: it renames the board “Knit” so you can pick it out on the mesh, stops broadcasting its position and node info, and stops relaying other radios' traffic to save battery.

It also marks the board “unmonitored”. Knit only reads Knit's own messages, so an ordinary Meshtastic message sent to this board would never reach you — the mark tells other people's apps that, instead of letting them write to a board nobody is reading.

Your board's own main channel is left alone and it stays on the public Meshtastic frequency, so other radios can still pass your messages along.

You can undo this at any time.
Board set up for Knit. It may reboot to apply this — it will reconnect on its own.

Set up on a dedicated frequency
Debug only. Pins the radio to slot %1$d instead of the public Meshtastic frequency.
Debug only. This board is already on a dedicated frequency, so Knit is using the full airtime allowance your region permits.
Debug only. Knit has no dedicated slot for this board\'s region, so this setup is unavailable here.
Set this board up on its own frequency?

Everything the normal setup does, plus the radio moves to a frequency only Knit boards use.

This is for places with no Meshtastic community nearby. You gain the whole airtime allowance your region permits instead of the tenth Knit normally limits itself to — but no stranger's radio will relay your messages any more, so only your own boards carry them.

Every board in your fleet must be set up this way to talk to the others. You can undo this at any time.

%1$s was last heard over the LoRa radio, not Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. Messages arrive slowly, long ones may not arrive, and photos are not sent until you are in radio range.

Private messages over LoRa are off

%1$s was last heard over the LoRa radio, not Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, and private messages are set to stay on the phone-to-phone radios. Turn on “Private messages over LoRa” in LoRa radio settings to reach them now.
Over LoRa only — airtime is used up, messages are delayed

%1$s can only be reached over the LoRa radio, and the radio has used its share of the airwaves for now. New messages wait their turn and arrive over the next few minutes; delivery ticks may take longer still.
LoRa airtime is used up — posts are slow to reach distant people

Some people here were last heard over the LoRa radio, and the radio has used its share of the airwaves for now. Everyone in Wi-Fi or Bluetooth range still gets your posts straight away; posts to the distant ones wait their turn and arrive over the next few minutes.
Group chats don\'t travel over LoRa — distant members get these later
Group chats don\'t travel over LoRa

The LoRa radio carries the Nearby room and private messages, not group chats. Someone here was last heard over LoRa, so they won\'t see these messages until they are back in Wi-Fi or Bluetooth range, or reachable through an Internet relay. Nothing is lost — the messages wait for them.
Long message — it may not reach people over LoRa
Public channel — names here are not verified

These posts were overheard by a paired Meshtastic radio on its public channel. Anyone with a radio can send them and anyone can claim any name, so treat both the names and the messages as unverified. Some arrive from the Internet rather than from anyone nearby. Knit reads this channel and does not post to it.
